Symbol Dictionary

¶6. Babel — Congregating for Convenience

Section 6 of 12 · ≈15 min

In This Section

The first post-flood act of the serpent's seed is to rebuild the city: "let us build us a city... lest we be scattered" is open defiance of "replenish the earth," and God answers the congregation with the very scattering it was built to prevent — naming the whole system Babel, CONFUSION, the name it carries all the way to Revelation.

The command Babel defies — "replenish the earth" — Gen. 9:1, 19:

  • Gen. 9:1. "And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth" — God's post-flood word is centrifugal: fill the earth, spread out. Every clause of Babel's manifesto is written against this one command; the whole plot is congregation against dispersal.
  • Gen. 9:19. "These are the three sons of Noah: and of them was the whole earth overspread" — God's design is that the whole earth be OVERSPREAD from Noah's sons. Scattering is the blessing, not the curse; the Babel-builders want the exact opposite.

The city is Cain's signature — and the Name is Seth's — Gen. 4:16-17, 26:

  • Gen. 4:16-17. "And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD... and he builded a city" — the first city-builder in Scripture is the first man who went out from the presence of the LORD. City-founding is the serpent-seed's signature act — safety and a name apart from God (the city of Cain is defined in “The Two Lineages — the City and the Name”); Babel is the same impulse resurrected after the flood.
  • Gen. 4:26. "then began men to call upon the name of the LORD" — Seth's line calls upon the NAME OF THE LORD. Set this exactly against Babel's "let us make us a name" (Gen. 11:4): the two seeds are divided by whose name is invoked — the Name called upon, or the name made.

Nimrod — the founder named — Gen. 10:8-12; Mic. 5:6:

  • Gen. 10:8-9. "And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth. He was a mighty hunter before the LORD" — the founder named: a mighty hunter before — in the face of — the LORD; might in defiance, not in worship.
  • Gen. 10:10. "And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar" — Babel is the HEADWATER: the first post-flood kingdom, founded by Nimrod son of Cush on the plain of Shinar in the first generations after the ark.
  • Gen. 10:11-12. "Out of that land went forth Asshur, and builded Nineveh" — from Shinar the city-system multiplies outward, city upon city compounding into "a great city" (Gen. 10:12). The confederacy of great cities is the fruit of Nimrod's Babel, and the pattern runs straight to "Babylon the great, that great city" of Revelation.
  • Mic. 5:6. "And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof" — Scripture itself calls the enemy-land "the land of Nimrod": the Bible's own witness that Nimrod's Babel names the archetypal oppressor-kingdom, the confederated power against God's people.

Down from the mountains to the plain of Shinar — Gen. 11:1-2:

  • Gen. 11:1. "And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech" — the pre-Babel condition: total unity of speech. Unity is not itself the sin; the sin is unity harnessed against the command of God.
  • Gen. 11:2. "as they journeyed from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar; and they dwelt there" — they stop journeying and settle on the plain: the geography of Cain's line, the lowland against the mountains of the faithful (see “The Two Lineages — the City and the Name”). To "dwell there" is to refuse to be scattered.
  • WitnessEP 70.3. White: "For a time, the descendants of Noah continued to dwell among the mountains where the ark had rested. As their numbers increased, apostasy led to division... After a time they decided to separate. Accordingly they journeyed to Shinar" — the mountain/plain division of the two classes re-enacted after the flood: the apostate line separates from the worshipers of God and descends to the plain.
  • Witness8MR 42.1. White: "Those who desired to forget their Creator, and to cast off the restraint of His law, decided to separate from the worshipers of God... Thus they hoped to make themselves independent of God" — the split named at its headwater: apostasy led to division, and Babel is the serpent-seed's congregation, built to be "independent of God."

Brick for stone, a tower for safety, a name for themselves — Gen. 11:3-4:

  • Gen. 11:3. "Go to, let us make brick, and burn them throughly. And they had brick for stone, and slime had they for morter" — man-made brick for God-made stone, slime for mortar: the whole enterprise is substitution, human manufacture standing in for what God provides — a self-made security.
  • Gen. 11:4. "Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth" — the manifesto in one verse: (1) "a city and a tower" — congregation for convenience and safety in numbers; (2) "make us a name" — self-exaltation against calling on the LORD's name (Gen. 4:26); (3) "lest we be scattered" — explicit defiance of Gen. 9:1. Every clause is against a word of God.
    • Babel / Babylon = the serpent-seed's confederated city-system: congregation for convenience and self-security in defiance of God's command to fill the earth, and self-naming in defiance of calling on the Name of the LORD (Gen. 11:4 against Gen. 9:1 and Gen. 4:26); founded by Nimrod on the plain of Shinar — "the beginning of his kingdom was Babel" (Gen. 10:10) — named CONFUSION by God's own judgment (Gen. 11:9), and carried by the Spirit to its end-time head as "BABYLON THE GREAT" (Rev. 17:5). Defined in full in the Symbol Dictionary.
    • the tower = man-made security against God's judgment and against God's command to scatter and fill the earth — brick-and-slime presumption trusted for the safety and the name that belong to the LORD alone, so small the LORD must "come down" to see it, answered by the very scattering it was built to prevent (Gen. 11:3-5; Gen. 11:8). Defined in full in the Symbol Dictionary.
  • WitnessPP 119.1. White: "One object before them in the erection of the tower was to secure their own safety in case of another deluge... The whole undertaking was designed to exalt still further the pride of its projectors and to turn the minds of future generations away from God and lead them into idolatry" — the tower-symbol confirmed exactly: man-made security against God's judgment, born of pride and unbelief in God's covenant word. The same paragraph supplies the seed-continuity: "their hearts, like that of Cain, rose up in rebellion against Him" (PP 119.1) — the Babel-builders' hearts are Cain's heart, one line from Cain's city (Gen. 4:17) to Nimrod's plain (see “The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall”).
  • WitnessEP 70.4. White: "God had directed men to disperse throughout the earth, but these Babel builders determined to keep their community united and to found a monarchy that should embrace the whole earth" — the defiance of Gen. 9:1 named: God said disperse; Babel said stay united and build a universal empire — the metropolis and the monument of its builders' power.

"Go to, let us go down" — the confederacy broken — Gen. 11:5-9:

  • Gen. 11:5. "And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded" — the tower that was to "reach unto heaven" is so small the LORD must "come down" to see it. The irony judges the pride: man cannot climb to God by masonry.
  • Gen. 11:6. "Behold, the people is one... and now nothing will be restrained from them, which they have imagined to do" — unbroken confederacy makes evil limitless. God scatters not from spite but to restrain corporate rebellion, as He divided the seeds at the first (see “The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall”).
  • Gen. 11:7. "Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language" — God answers "Go to, let us build" with His own "Go to, let us go down." The confounding of speech is the instrument of the scattering the builders feared.
  • Gen. 11:8. "So the LORD scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city" — the exact thing they built to prevent, God accomplishes. The distinction between the two classes is remade by judgment, as at Eden's gate and at the flood.
  • Gen. 11:9. "Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the LORD did there confound the language of all the earth" — they sought a name; God gave them one — Babel, CONFUSION. The self-made name becomes the byword of judgment, and this naming is inherited by the whole city-system of Revelation.
  • WitnessEP 71.1. White: "Angels were sent to bring to naught the purpose of the builders... the language was confounded so that the directions delivered were often the reverse of those that had been given... Lightnings from heaven as an evidence of God's displeasure broke off the upper portion of the tower" — corroborates Gen. 11:7-8: God's direct judgment confounds the speech and breaks the tower, accomplishing the scattering the builders built against.

From Babel to Babylon the great — the city-system at full stature — Rev. 17:5; 18:4:

  • Rev. 17:5. "And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH" — the headwater of Shinar grown to the end-time confederacy of the serpent's seed: still self-named, still congregated against God, and Scripture names her by Babel's name — "the mother" of the whole system.
  • WitnessTMR 37.2. Andrews: "The word Babylon signifies confusion, and is derived from Babel... being the chosen term of the Holy Spirit to designate 'that mighty city'... was doubtless selected with especial reference to its signification" — the pioneer definition sealing the Babel-to-Babylon line: Babylon = confusion = Babel, the Spirit's own chosen name for the Revelation city, "composed of professed worshipers of God."
  • WitnessTMR 47.2. Andrews: "Since the great apostasy, the majority of the professed followers have busied themselves in attempting to climb up to heaven some other way. They have been confounded in the attempt, and scattered abroad... with creeds as discordant as the languages of those who were dispersed at the ancient tower" — the antitype drawn: the great apostasy repeats Babel's tower, climbing to heaven another way, and ends in the same confusion.
  • Rev. 18:4. "Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues" — the final answer to Babel's "lest we be scattered": God still scatters His people OUT of the city of confusion before He judges it — the everlasting separation of the two seeds (see “Come Out, My People — the Pilgrim Call”).

Synthesis

DEFINITION — BABEL — CONGREGATING FOR CONVENIENCE = the first post-flood act of the serpent's seed is to rebuild the city, and every clause of the rebuilding is written against a word of God. God's blessing was centrifugal — "replenish the earth" (Gen. 9:1), the whole earth "overspread" from Noah's sons (Gen. 9:19) — but the apostate line, hearts "like that of Cain" (PP 119.1; Gen. 4:16-17), separated from the worshipers of God, descended from the mountains to the plain of Shinar (Gen. 11:2; EP 70.3; 8MR 42.1), and under Nimrod, the mighty hunter before the LORD whose kingdom began at Babel (Gen. 10:8-10; Mic. 5:6), raised a city and a tower of brick and slime (Gen. 11:3): congregation for convenience ("let us build us a city"), self-exaltation against the Name called upon by Seth's line ("let us make us a name," Gen. 11:4 against Gen. 4:26), and open defiance of the scattering ("lest we be scattered abroad"). The tower was man-made security against God's judgment and monument to its builders' pride (PP 119.1; EP 70.4) — yet so small the LORD must "come down" to see it (Gen. 11:5). Because unbroken confederacy makes evil limitless (Gen. 11:6), God answered "let us build" with "let us go down" (Gen. 11:7), confounded the speech, broke the tower (EP 71.1), and accomplished by judgment the very scattering the congregation was built to prevent — the distinction between the two classes remade, as at Eden's gate and at the flood, and the self-made name turned to CONFUSION: Babel (Gen. 11:8-9). That name the Spirit carries to the end: the city-system of Shinar reaches full stature as "BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS" (Rev. 17:5; TMR 37.2), the great apostasy repeating the tower — climbing to heaven another way, confounded into discordant creeds (TMR 47.2) — until God's final answer to "lest we be scattered" falls: "Come out of her, my people" (Rev. 18:4). The witnesses repeat: the serpent's seed congregates for convenience; God's people are content to be scattered at His word — the same drama replayed inside one family in "Abraham and Lot — the Tent and the Plain," and consummated in "Come Out, My People — the Pilgrim Call."

Symbols Defined Here

  • Babel / Babylon = the serpent-seed's confederated city-system: congregation for convenience and self-security in defiance of God's command to fill the earth, and self-naming in defiance of calling on the Name of the LORD; founded by Nimrod on the plain of Shinar, named CONFUSION by God's judgment, and carried forward by the Spirit to "Babylon the great" (Gen. 11:4; Gen. 11:8-9; Gen. 10:8-10; Gen. 9:1; Gen. 4:26; Rev. 17:5).
  • the tower = man-made security against God's judgment and against His command to scatter and fill the earth — brick-and-slime presumption trusted for the safety and the name that belong to the LORD alone, exposed by the LORD's "coming down" and answered by the confusion of tongues and the very scattering it was built to prevent (Gen. 11:3-5; Gen. 11:8).

Symbols Carried

the seed of the serpent and the enmity — the God-put division Babel's confederacy tries to erase, mercifully remade by judgment (see “The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall”); the city of Cain, calling on the name of the LORD, and the mountains-and-plains geography of the two classes, all resurrected at Shinar (see “The Two Lineages — the City and the Name”); the distinction remade by judgment, as at the flood (see “The Days of Noah — the Institutions of Eden Under Attack”); Babel's plain becomes the plain toward which Lot pitches his tent (see “Abraham and Lot — the Tent and the Plain”), and Babylon the great receives her final sentence and the last call of separation (see “The Seal or the Mark — the Distinction Made Visible” and "Come Out, My People — the Pilgrim Call").

For Discussion

  1. Babel says "let us make us a name" (Gen. 11:4) while Seth's line "began... to call upon the name of the LORD" (Gen. 4:26) — the two classes divided by whose name is invoked. Where in your own life or in the church do we build a name for ourselves — reputation, platform, institution, security — where God is asking us to call on His?
  2. The builders congregated "lest we be scattered" (Gen. 11:4) in direct defiance of "replenish the earth" (Gen. 9:1) — safety in numbers, convenience over command. What forms of congregating for convenience look reasonable to us today, and how do we test whether a gathering is unity in God's word or a confederacy against it (Gen. 11:6)?
  3. God's final answer to "lest we be scattered" is "Come out of her, my people" (Rev. 18:4). If God still scatters His people out of the city of confusion before He judges it, what would it mean this week to accept the scattering rather than the tower — to come out in body and in spirit now, while the call is mercy and not yet plague?
